final.title: What capacity limits usually hide
final.body:
Capacity limits usually hide in one repeatable workflow decision: do you keep answering the same customer questions by hand, or do you build a bounded system for the routine part and keep judgment with you?

For a small business owner, that is the real comparison. It is not “AI or no AI.” It is manual work, another hire, or a narrow automation investment.

The quickest test is simple: are the requests mostly the same few patterns, or is every case genuinely different? If you can group the work into a small set of common questions, AI may help with the standard part. If each case needs live judgment, context, or a human call, forcing automation is the wrong move.

That is the kind of workflow Bareni looks at in a diagnostic. We identify one recurring process, say honestly whether AI fits, and—if it does—define a small pilot with scope, fixed price, and measures. Human approval stays in place for money movement and other high-risk decisions.

The point is not to AI everything. It is to find the boring process that keeps sitting on the desk and decide whether it is the bottleneck.
